task: EPMCDME-8559 — make the FilesDropzone remove-file control a real accessible Button (role, per-file accessible name, keyboard focus ring, focus restoration after removal) and mark decorative icons aria-hidden on the other file-delete controls.

key_reasoning.reason: 8 files changed across 3 directories (src/components, src/components/form/FilesDropzone/components, src/pages/skills/components). No new production files; 4 of the 8 are test files carrying 18 new tests, so the raw file count overstates production scope — actual production delta is ~45 lines in File.tsx, FileList.tsx, FileListItem.tsx and SkillBundleFilesSection.tsx.

The WCAG success criteria (4.1.2 name/role/value, 1.1.1 non-text content) are precise, but the ticket did not enumerate the follow-on obligations that two rounds of code review surfaced (4 major findings): visible focus ring, focus restoration after row removal, and section-qualified accessible names so an uploaded and a newly selected file with the same name stay distinguishable. Scope grew after the first implementation pass.

Base risk is low — the shared Button component and aria-label conventions already existed, and every change is trivially reversible. The only non-boilerplate logic is the focus-restoration effect in FileList, which reads live DOM buttons via listRef.querySelectorAll and clamps a pending index against the re-rendered row count; it is index-based rather than ref-based and depends on the delete buttons being the only buttons inside the list container. Bumped one tier for the accessibility-compliance driver.

Four UI components touched (FileListItem gains a fileKind prop, FileList gains focus state, File.tsx and SkillBundleFilesSection get aria-hidden on decorative icons). All presentational, single layer, no shared contract broken.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from S (2) to M (3): accessibility-compliance requirement (WCAG 4.1.2 / 1.1.1 conformance is the reason for the ticket).
